comment:
MCP traffic arriving on the public external door (cmuir-mcp.ping-devops.com) from an agent like ChatGPT, Claude or LM Studio. Selected by HOST, not by path: the path is the same '^/mcp' that mcp-olb-primary matches, and the two differ only in who is calling and which authorization server issued the token. Name sorts before 'mcp-olb-*' so IG picks this route first for that host; every other host falls through to the existing routes unchanged.

The token is issued by oauth-mcp's OWN embedded authorization server (RFC 7591 registration or CIMD), not by PingOne — an external client cannot get a PingOne token because PingOne has no dynamic client registration. So this route cannot reuse the PingOne introspection resolver in config.json, and it must not use jwks-token-validation.groovy either: that script hard-requires iss == PINGONE_ISSUER_URI (deny 'issuer_mismatch') and a 'gateway:mcp:invoke' scope, and widening it would change the shared validator every other MCP route depends on.

Instead this route introspects the token against the AS that actually issued it — oauth-mcp's own RFC 7662 endpoint. That validates the token AND populates the OAuth2Context that p1az-decision.groovy reads for subject and scope; without a resource-server filter that context is empty and P1AZ would score an identity-less request. The Authorization header is deliberately NOT exchanged or replaced, so mcp-server independently validates the same bearer on arrival (HttpMCPTransport's RFC 9207 issuer check accepts the embedded issuer) — the gateway authorizes, the MCP server authenticates, and neither trusts the other's word for it.
name: mcp-external-door
condition: ${find(request.uri.path, '^/mcp(?!/invest|/weather)') and not empty request.headers['Host'] and find(request.headers['Host'][0], '^cmuir-mcp[.]ping-devops[.]com')}

heap.comment: oauth-mcp's embedded AS introspection endpoint (RFC 7662). It takes no client authentication, so a plain ClientHandler is enough — unlike the PingOne resolver in config.json, which has to inject client_id/client_secret.
heap.name: ExternalDoorTokenResolver

heap.comment: mcp:invoke is what DCR_OPEN_REGISTRATION_SCOPE grants a self-registered client ('mcp:invoke read'). Do NOT require gateway:mcp:invoke here — that is the internal BFF-to-gateway scope and no external client will ever hold it.
heap.name: ExternalDoorResourceServerFilter
